opening.argument: The material is a warning to Netflix customers, supported by an investigation in which Segura used a computer stripped of personal information and recorded what happened. The report describes an email or pop-up leading to a fake Netflix sign-in page, then attributes the requests for remote access and credit-card information to the caller Segura tested. Those steps are presented as the subject of the investigation, not as directions for viewers to follow or an offer from the video. The report also qualifies the threat's current status: Netflix believed the activity was no longer active, while Segura warned it could recur under other company names. It does not establish that customers granted access or lost money.

citations.quote: The Better Business Bureau is warning Netflix customers about a scam.
Segura set up computer stripped of personal information and recorded the screen as he investigated the scam.
Netflix customers get an email or pop-up ad directing them to a real looking but fake Netflix log-in page.
When the Scammer asked for credit card information, Segura ended the call.
Netflix told us, they believe the scam is no longer active, but Segura warns con artists could try it again, posing as other companies.
